title: F1: Horner Ahead of Cadillac Hammer? Clarity Revealed
text:
Cadillac has officially shut down rumors linking Christian Horner to its Formula 1 project. This comes after speculation intensified following Horner’s departure from Red Bull.
F1 insider Nelson Valkenburg had previously suggested on the “Nailing the Apex” podcast that Horner might land with either Alpine or Cadillac, keeping him in the Formula 1 spotlight.
Cadillac Denies Horner Rumors While an Italian portal reported that negotiations were underway between Horner and Cadillac, the company’s CEO, Dan Towriss, has clarified the situation. “I would like to officially get this rumor out of the world,” Towriss stated. “There were no conversations with Christian Horner and there are no planned.”
Instead, Cadillac is focused squarely on its own burgeoning Formula 1 endeavor. The team has already secured experienced drivers Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez, viewing their leadership and feedback as crucial for the project’s success. Mick Schumacher, however, has not found a place within the team.
Graeme Lowdon Leads Cadillac’s Formula 1 Team Cadillac is building its Formula 1 team with Graeme Lowdon at the helm as its permanent team boss. Lowdon expressed his confidence in Bottas and Perez, calling their contributions “invaluable to bring this team to life.” He emphasized that their experience will be strategically used to shape the team’s structure.
The commitment to experienced drivers like Bottas and Perez signals Cadillac’s clear ambition for long-term success in Formula 1. With a structured approach under Lowdon, Cadillac appears to be laying a solid foundation for its upcoming F1 season, seemingly without Christian Horner.
